high.title: Mutable PendingIntent wraps an implicit Intent
high.description: A PendingIntent is created without FLAG_IMMUTABLE around a base Intent that names no component, so whoever receives it can choose where it goes and what it carries. The app creates a mutable PendingIntent wrapping an implicit Intent (action 'santos.cs.ksu.myServ') and leaks it to any app on the device via an implicit broadcast with the action 'santos.cs.ksu.edu.benignpireceiver'.
high.impact: An attacker app can intercept the PendingIntent and modify its underlying Intent to target the non-exported 'MySensitiveService' (action 'santos.cs.ksu.sensitiveServ'), bypassing the 'android:exported="false"' restriction and executing privileged actions.

lines_html: button.setOnClickListener(new android.view.View.OnClickListener() { // from class: edu.cs.ksu.benign.MainActivity.1
public void onClick(android.view.View v) {
android.os.Bundle bundle = new android.os.Bundle();
android.app.PendingIntent pi = android.app.PendingIntent.getService(edu.cs.ksu.benign.MainActivity.this.getApplicationContext(), 0, new android.content.Intent("santos.cs.ksu.myServ"), 134217728);
bundle.putParcelable("pendingIntent", pi);
android.content.Intent intent = new android.content.Intent("santos.cs.ksu.edu.benignpireceiver");
intent.putExtra("bundle", bundle);
edu.cs.ksu.benign.MainActivity.this.sendBroadcast(intent);

high.recommendation: Give the base Intent an explicit component and add FLAG_IMMUTABLE; use FLAG_MUTABLE only where the receiver must fill in extras, and then still with an explicit component.

warnings: PendingIntent mutability defaults changed at API 31; confirm the app's targetSdkVersion.

medium.title: Unprotected broadcast with action 'santos.cs.ksu.edu.benignpireceiver'
medium.description: The application sends an unprotected broadcast with the action 'santos.cs.ksu.edu.benignpireceiver' containing a PendingIntent in its extras. Any application on the device can register a receiver for this action and obtain the PendingIntent, allowing it to trigger the non-exported 'MyService' with the privileges of the benign app.

low.title: Task hijacking possible on Android 10 and lower
low.description: MainActivity is an exported activity that does not specify android:taskAffinity, making it susceptible to task hijacking (StrandHogg) on older Android versions.
low.impact: A malicious app can place its own activity on top of MainActivity, potentially phishing for user credentials or sensitive information.
low.recommendation: Set android:taskAffinity to an empty string or a unique value to isolate the task.

reasons: The finding does not establish that the activity displays sensitive information.

info.title: Application is debuggable in this build
info.description: android:debuggable="true" lets any user with adb attach a debugger to the process, read and modify memory, and inspect application data. The application is marked as debuggable, which can allow an attacker with physical access or root to attach a debugger and inspect the application's memory and execution flow. The application is marked as debuggable in the AndroidManifest.xml.
info.impact: An attacker with physical access or a malicious app on the same device can attach a debugger to the process, inspect memory, and potentially extract sensitive data.
info.recommendation: Remove android:debuggable or set it to "false" for release builds.

reasons: Debuggable release build. A debuggable build is a release-pipeline defect rather than an exploitable flaw - attaching a debugger already requires ADB access to the device. Worth fixing, not worth a severity.
Attaching a debugger requires ADB access, making this a build-process defect rather than a vulnerability.

info.title: Missing screenshot protection on sensitive screen
info.description: The app does not set FLAG_SECURE in SenitiveActivity, which is intended to show sensitive information.
info.impact: Screen contents can be captured via screenshots or screen recording apps.

lines_html: /* JADX INFO: loaded from: classes.dex */
public class SenitiveActivity extends android.support.v7.app.AppCompatActivity {
@Override // android.support.v7.app.AppCompatActivity, android.support.v4.app.FragmentActivity, android.support.v4.app.SupportActivity, android.app.Activity
protected void onCreate(android.os.Bundle savedInstanceState) {
setContentView(edu.ksu.cs.benign.R.layout.activity_senitive);

reasons: Screen contents not protected from capture. Without FLAG_SECURE, what a screen shows can end up in screenshots, screen recordings and the task-switcher preview. That matters on screens showing credentials, card numbers or balances; on its own it is a hardening note.
Screen contents not protected from capture reaches at most CVSS 3.3 (Low); the vector given scores this finding above anything the class does.
The finding does not prove the activity displays sensitive data such as credentials or account numbers.

info.title: No network security config declared
info.description: The app declares neither android:networkSecurityConfig nor usesCleartextTraffic, so it relies on platform defaults and pins no domain. With targetSdkVersion 27 those defaults still permit cleartext HTTP (see the cleartext finding).
info.impact: Without pinning, anyone who gets a CA trusted on the device can read and alter the app's TLS traffic.
info.recommendation: Declare a network security config that disables cleartext and pins the domains that carry sensitive traffic.

reasons: No certificate pinning. Pinning defends against an attacker who already controls a trusted CA or the device's trust store. Without one of those, TLS is still doing its job. It becomes a finding when paired with what the unpinned channel actually carries.
Lack of certificate pinning is a hardening note that requires a sensitive data channel to be a vulnerability.

info.title: targetSdkVersion 27 allows implicit component export
info.description: On targetSdk 27, any component with an intent-filter is exported unless it says otherwise.
info.recommendation: Raise targetSdkVersion to 31+ and declare android:exported explicitly on every filtered component.

reasons: Legacy platform behaviour from SDK levels. An SDK level is a statement about which platform defaults apply, not a defect. It is context for the findings that depend on those defaults - pair it with one of them.
This is a documented platform default that requires a specific vulnerable component to be impactful.
warnings: Implicit export only applies below targetSdk 31; confirm the app's targetSdkVersion before treating this as exploitable.

info.title: Task hijacking (StrandHogg) possible on Android 10 and lower
info.description: minSdkVersion 22 lets the app run on Android versions before 11, and its task affinity is its package name "edu.ksu.cs.benign". There, another app can declare the same affinity, with allowTaskReparenting, and have its own activity shown in this app's task.
info.impact: On a device running Android 10 or lower, a malicious app can put a look-alike screen on top of this app's task, phishing credentials or keeping the real app from being shown.
info.recommendation: Raise minSdkVersion to 30, where Android fixed this. Until then, android:taskAffinity="" on the <application> mitigates the original attack, though not its runtime variant on unpatched Android 9 and lower.

reasons: The finding does not establish that the activity displays sensitive information. Kept at Informational: the CVSS vector, scored for an attacker with local access and high privileges, still gives Low.
